jurisdiction.name: International AI summits and declarations
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: Since 2023, governments have adopted a series of AI declarations at summits without a standing secretariat. The AI safety summit series (Bletchley 2023, Seoul 2024, Paris 2025, New Delhi 2026) produced political declarations on frontier AI risks, safety institutes, inclusion and sustainability. The REAIM summits (The Hague 2023, Seoul 2024, A Coruña 2026) and a Paris declaration address responsible military use of AI. None of these texts is legally binding.
lead_institutions: Republic of Korea and UK (AI Seoul Summit 2024)
Presidency of the French Republic (AI Action Summit 2025)
Netherlands, Republic of Korea and Spain (REAIM summits)
International Network of AI Safety Institutes

instruments.official_title: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023
instruments.english_title: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Safety Summit (hosted by the United Kingdom, Bletchley Park)
instruments.publisher_name: AI Safety Summit (hosted by the United Kingdom, Bletchley Park)
instruments.summary: Declaration of governments attending the first AI Safety Summit. It affirms that AI should be designed, developed and used in a safe, human-centric, trustworthy and responsible way, identifies particular safety risks from frontier AI (including misuse, loss of control, cybersecurity, biotechnology and disinformation), states that developers of the most capable systems bear a strong responsibility for safety testing, and sets an agenda of shared scientific understanding of risks, risk-based national policies, an international network of frontier AI safety research, and further summits.
instruments.current_status: Declaration of the countries represented at the AI Safety Summit, first published by the UK Government on 1 November 2023 (page last updated 13 February 2025). The European Union is listed among those represented; the page notes New Zealand joined on 23 October 2024.
instruments.evidence_reference: GOV.UK collection page: Published 1 November 2023, Last updated 13 February 2025 ('Updated to include New Zealand as a signatory'). Signatory list read from the declaration page (28 countries + EU), plus NZ per change history. 'Kingdom of Saudi Arabia' -> SAU. | Independent check 2026-10-21: current_status: page says New Zealand joined on 23 October 2024 (page last updated 13 Feb 2025), not 'added 13 February 2025'; page does not say 'non-binding'

instruments.official_title: Seoul Declaration for safe, innovative and inclusive AI by participants attending the Leaders' Session: AI Seoul Summit, 21 May 2024
instruments.english_title: Seoul Declaration for safe, innovative and inclusive AI
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Seoul Summit, Leaders' Session (co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom)
instruments.publisher_name: AI Seoul Summit, Leaders' Session (co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom)
instruments.summary: Leaders' declaration that treats AI safety, innovation and inclusivity as interlinked goals. It calls for deeper international cooperation and interoperable governance frameworks, supports existing and planned AI safety institutes, research programmes and oversight bodies, encourages a risk-based approach that respects human rights and supports sustainable development, and calls for coordination with the UN, G7, G20, OECD and other forums. It welcomes the companion Seoul Statement of Intent on AI safety science.
instruments.current_status: Declaration of the participants in the Leaders' Session of the AI Seoul Summit, published by the UK Government on 21 May 2024. The European Union is listed among the parties represented.
instruments.evidence_reference: GOV.UK page: Published 21 May 2024. Participants named in para 1: 10 countries + EU. | Independent check 2026-10-21: text does not say 'non-binding'

instruments.official_title: Seoul Statement of Intent toward International Cooperation on AI Safety Science, AI Seoul Summit 2024 (Annex)
instruments.english_title: Seoul Statement of Intent toward International Cooperation on AI Safety Science
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Seoul Summit, Leaders' Session (co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom)
instruments.publisher_name: AI Seoul Summit, Leaders' Session (co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom)
instruments.summary: Annex to the Seoul Declaration in which leaders state their intent to cooperate on the science of AI safety. It welcomes the creation of AI safety institutes and similar publicly backed bodies, and sets the aim of building a shared scientific understanding of AI risks, aligning research, testing and evaluation methods, and forming an international network of such institutions, on the basis of openness, transparency and reciprocity.
instruments.current_status: Statement of intent annexed to the Seoul Declaration, published by the UK Government on 21 May 2024. The European Union is listed among the parties.
instruments.evidence_reference: GOV.UK page: Published 21 May 2024; same 10 countries + EU named. | Independent check 2026-10-21: text does not say 'non-binding'

instruments.official_title: Seoul Ministerial Statement for advancing AI safety, innovation and inclusivity: AI Seoul Summit 2024
instruments.english_title: Seoul Ministerial Statement for advancing AI safety, innovation and inclusivity
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Seoul Summit, Ministers' Session (co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom)
instruments.publisher_name: AI Seoul Summit, Ministers' Session (co-hosted by the Republic of Korea and the United Kingdom)
instruments.summary: Statement by ministers attending the AI Seoul Summit covering three linked priorities. On safety, it addresses risks from frontier AI and the role of AI safety institutes and commits to work towards defining thresholds for severe risks ahead of the next summit in France. On innovation, it supports AI ecosystems, public-sector use and energy-efficient AI. On inclusivity, it calls for equitable access to AI's benefits and participation by developing countries.
instruments.current_status: Statement of ministers from the Ministers' Session of the AI Seoul Summit on 22 May 2024, published by the UK Government the same day. The representative of the European Union is listed among the ministers.
instruments.evidence_reference: GOV.UK page: Published 22 May 2024. Preamble names ministers of 27 countries + EU representative. | Independent check 2026-10-21: text does not say 'non-binding'; page does not say 'adopted'

instruments.official_title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
instruments.english_title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Seoul Summit (published by the UK Government)
instruments.publisher_name: AI Seoul Summit (published by the UK Government)
instruments.summary: Voluntary commitments by frontier AI developers announced at the AI Seoul Summit. Signatory organisations commit to identify, assess and manage risks across the model lifecycle, to publish safety frameworks focused on severe risks before the AI summit in France, to set thresholds at which risks would be intolerable and not to develop or deploy a model if mitigations cannot keep risks below them, and to be accountable and transparent to external actors including governments.
instruments.current_status: Voluntary commitments by AI organisations, first published by the UK Government on 21 May 2024. The page (last updated 7 February 2025) lists 20 organisations, including four added to the original list.
instruments.evidence_reference: GOV.UK collection page: Published 21 May 2024, Last updated 7 Feb 2025 ('Additional organisations added'). 20 companies listed (Amazon, Anthropic, Cohere, Google, G42, IBM, Inflection AI, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral AI, Naver, OpenAI, Samsung Electronics, TII, xAI, Zhipu.ai, Magic, Minimax, 01.ai, NVIDIA). | Independent check 2026-10-21: page gives no date for the added signatories; 7 Feb 2025 is only the page's last-updated date

instruments.official_title: Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet
instruments.english_title: Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Action Summit (hosted by France, co-chaired by India), Paris
instruments.publisher_name: AI Action Summit (hosted by France, co-chaired by India), Paris
instruments.summary: Outcome statement of the AI Action Summit. Signatories set priorities to promote AI accessibility and reduce digital divides, ensure AI is open, inclusive, transparent, ethical, safe, secure and trustworthy, foster innovation, shape the future of work positively, make AI sustainable for people and planet, and reinforce international cooperation on AI governance. It welcomes a Public Interest AI Platform and Incubator, an observatory on AI's energy impact with the International Energy Agency, and a network of observatories on AI and work. It covers civil uses of AI only.
instruments.current_status: Statement published by the Élysée on 11 February 2025. The African Union Commission and the European Union appear in the list of signatories.
instruments.evidence_reference: Elysee page 'Posted on 11 February 2025'. Signatory list read from page: 63 states + AUC + EU. Footnote 1: statement covers civil applications only. French version: https://www.elysee.fr/emmanuel-macron/2025/02/11/declaration-sur-une-intelligence-artificielle-inclusive-et-durable-pour-les-peuples-et-la-planete | Independent check 2026-10-21: page does not say 'non-binding'

instruments.official_title: Paris Declaration on Maintaining Human Control in AI enabled Weapon Systems
instruments.english_title: Paris Declaration on Maintaining Human Control in AI enabled Weapon Systems
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Action Summit, Paris (published by the Presidency of the French Republic)
instruments.publisher_name: AI Action Summit, Paris (published by the Presidency of the French Republic)
instruments.summary: Declaration on military uses of AI made alongside the AI Action Summit. Endorsing states commit to develop and use AI in the military domain responsibly and in line with international law, including international humanitarian law; to keep humans responsible and accountable, with safeguards preserving human judgement over the use of force; not to allow autonomous weapon systems operating outside human control and command to make life-and-death decisions; and to support continued international dialogue on the subject.
instruments.current_status: Declaration published by the Élysée on 11 February 2025 under its AI Action Summit dossier; the page lists 27 endorsing states.
instruments.evidence_reference: Elysee page 'Publié le 11 février 2025'; endorsing list read from page (27 states, French names). Summit results PDF mentions '64 signatories' for commitments on human control, inconsistent with the page; page list used. | Independent check 2026-10-21: page does not say 'non-binding'

instruments.english_title: New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact
instruments.issuing_authority: AI Impact Summit (hosted by India), New Delhi
instruments.publisher_name: AI Impact Summit (hosted by India), New Delhi
instruments.summary: Outcome declaration of the AI Impact Summit, headed New Delhi, 18-19 February 2026. Referring to the summit's three Sutras, it supports cooperation across seven Chakras (pillars): democratising AI resources; economic growth and social good; secure and trusted AI; AI for science; access for social empowerment; human capital; and resilience, innovation and efficiency. It notes the voluntary Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI and the Voluntary Guiding Principles on Resilient, Innovative and Efficient AI.
instruments.current_status: Declaration adopted at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi (header dated 18-19 February 2026) and announced by PIB on 21 February 2026. The page lists 92 endorsing countries and international organisations as of 5 March 2026, including the European Union and IFAD.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text is annexed to PIB release posted 21 FEB 2026 (Ministry of Electronics & IT); annex headed 'AI Impact Summit Declaration', New Delhi, 18-19 February 2026; endorsers table 'as of 5th March 2026' (92 entries: 90 states + EU + IFAD). Publication_date = PIB posting date (no single adoption date printed). PIB 24 Feb 2026 release (PRID=2232005) records Bangladesh, Costa Rica, Guatemala joining. Summit outcome page https://impact.indiaai.gov.in/outcome-resources is JS-rendered (no links readable). | Independent check 2026-10-21: 'non-binding' is said of the Charter and other initiatives, not of the declaration itself; summary names the three Sutras (People, Planet, Progress), which the page does not name, and paraphrases the seven pillars inaccurately ('trustworthy AI', 'energy-efficient AI'); release dated 21 Feb 2026; declaration header reads New Delhi 18-19 February 2026

instruments.english_title: REAIM 2023 Call to Action (Responsible AI in the Military Domain)
instruments.issuing_authority: Summit on Responsible Artificial Intelligence in the Military Domain (REAIM 2023), The Hague (hosted by the Netherlands, co-hosted by the Republic of Korea)
instruments.publisher_name: Summit on Responsible Artificial Intelligence in the Military Domain (REAIM 2023), The Hague (hosted by the Netherlands, co-hosted by the Republic of Korea)
instruments.summary: Call to action agreed by government representatives at the first REAIM summit. It recognises the opportunities of AI in the military domain and its risks, including unreliability, unclear accountability and unintended escalation; stresses that humans remain responsible for decisions, that AI use must comply with international law, and that data governance and training are needed; and invites states and other stakeholders to share good practices, develop national frameworks and continue an inclusive multistakeholder dialogue.
instruments.current_status: Joint call to action agreed by government representatives at the REAIM 2023 summit and published by the Government of the Netherlands (February 2023).
instruments.evidence_reference: government.nl page dated 16-02-2023. Endorsers from 'REAIM 2023 Endorsing Countries and Territories' (government.nl, dated 04-04-2025) PDF: 58 entries incl. Palestine (PSE); 'Northern Macedonia' -> MKD. | Independent check 2026-10-21: page/PDF do not say 'non-binding' and print no list of endorsing states; no date printed on page or PDF; 2023-02-16 comes from the government.nl URL path (acceptable); Korea co-host role not stated on page or PDF

instruments.official_title: A Coruña Declaration: "REAIM 2026 Pathways to Action"
instruments.english_title: A Coruña Declaration: REAIM Pathways to Action
instruments.issuing_authority: Third Summit on Responsible Artificial Intelligence in the Military Domain (REAIM 2026), A Coruña (hosted by Spain)
instruments.publisher_name: Third Summit on Responsible Artificial Intelligence in the Military Domain (REAIM 2026), A Coruña (hosted by Spain)
instruments.summary: Outcome document of the third REAIM summit, building on The Hague Call to Action and the Seoul Blueprint for Action. It sets out practical measures for responsible military AI: building responsibility in from the outset, keeping human judgement central, rigorous testing, legal reviews, clear accountability and voluntary confidence-building measures. It also calls for national focal points, capacity-building for developing countries and closer work with industry on human-machine interfaces.
instruments.current_status: Outcome declaration of REAIM 2026, published by Spain's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which lists 45 endorsing countries and states that it remains open to approval by other countries.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF has no printed date. Summit dates 4-5 Feb 2026 from MAEC press note dated 5 Feb 2026 (Exteriores clausura en A Coruña...). Endorser list (45) read from the REAIM2026 page ('As of today', undated). Date given as month only. | Independent check 2026-10-21: page and PDF do not print the summit dates (4-5 February 2026) or say 'non-binding'; PDF is headed 'REAIM Pathways to Action'; no date printed on either page or PDF (2026-02 not directly confirmed, only '2026')

instruments.official_title: International Network of AI Safety Institutes - Mission Statement
instruments.english_title: International Network of AI Safety Institutes: Mission Statement
instruments.issuing_authority: International Network of AI Safety Institutes (convened by the United States, San Francisco)
instruments.publisher_name: International Network of AI Safety Institutes (convened by the United States, San Francisco)
instruments.summary: Joint mission statement launching the International Network of AI Safety Institutes, building on the Seoul Statement of Intent. Members commit to bring together technical expertise to build a common understanding of AI safety risks and mitigations, promote interoperable principles and best practices, and help countries at all stages of development benefit from AI. Initial priority areas are research, testing (including joint testing exercises), common approaches to interpreting tests of advanced AI systems, and global inclusion and information sharing.
instruments.current_status: Joint statement of the AI safety institutes and government offices of the founding members, launched on 21 November 2024; non-binding. The European Union (European Commission) is also a member.
instruments.evidence_reference: NIST document page: text says members 'have gathered today in San Francisco on November 21, 2024'. Commerce fact sheet dated November 20, 2024 (https://www.commerce.gov/news/fact-sheets/2024/11/fact-sheet-us-department-commerce-us-department-state-launch-international) lists the 10 members. Signatories are member governments represented by their institutes.

instruments.official_title: Hiroshima AI Process Friends Group Action Plan 2026
instruments.english_title: Hiroshima AI Process Friends Group Action Plan 2026
instruments.summary: Action plan of the Friends Group, a voluntary framework of countries supporting the Hiroshima AI Process, drawn up after its second in-person meeting in Tokyo. It sets out joint initiatives in two areas: co-promoting AI governance (workshops on the OECD AI Principles and the HAIP Reporting Framework, capacity building, research on interoperability of frameworks) and co-advancing AI deployment (sharing use cases and building AI skills, including talent programmes for Global South countries), with projects led by individual members and partner organisations.
instruments.current_status: Voluntary action plan of the Hiroshima AI Process Friends Group (66 countries and regions), dated 16 March 2026 and updated on 27 April 2026.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF dated March 16, 2026, 'Updated on April 27, 2026'. Plan text refers to 66 countries and regions; signatories = Friends Group membership list on https://www.soumu.go.jp/hiroshimaaiprocess/en/supporters.html (as of August 2026: 69 states + EU). Friends Group launched May 2024 as 'a voluntary framework of countries supporting the spirit of the Hiroshima AI Process' - no separate founding text found on the page; G7 HAIP documents themselves belong to G7. | Independent check 2026-10-21: corrected from the official source.
